title: Cedar Edge - Growth & Regional Provisioning Review
next_steps: Redwood to send revised 12-month pricing and reserved capacity options by 2027-03-25
Customer to confirm target regions and expected Q3-Q4 token volumes by 2027-03-29
Schedule 30-min technical validation with Cedar Edge SREs and Redwood SEs (Diego) week of 2027-03-29

Diego Morales: Prepare latency benchmark plan and private deployment checklist by 2027-03-26
Maya Patel: Share current request distribution and region priority list by 2027-03-29
Sara Yamada: Initiate procurement paperwork and share PO/contract timeline by 2027-04-02
header:
Date: 2027-03-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood attendees: Ava Chen (AE), Diego Morales (SE)
Cedar Edge attendees: Maya Patel (Head Infra), Liam O'Connor (VP ML), Sara Yamada (Procurement), Tom Reilly (SRE)
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion checkpoint. Customer confirmed growth trajectory (2.5x tokens next 12 months), wants to add EU (Frankfurt) and APAC (Singapore) regions, prefers a reserved capacity + burst mix. Procurement timeline for contract extension targeting April PO. Key blockers: SOC2 evidence, KMS integration details, and latency SLOs for EU traffic. Agreed next steps and technical validation plan.
topics: Reserved capacity sizing and burst policies
Regional provisioning (EU + APAC) and data residency
Contract extension timing and pricing structure
Compliance: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, RBAC
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you folks squeezing this in. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya (Cedar Edge): Hey, Maya here.
[00:10] Liam (Cedar Edge): Liam on.
[00:12] Sara (Cedar Edge): Sara here.
[00:15] Diego (Redwood SE): Diego here, good to see you.
[00:18] Tom (Cedar Edge): Tom, SRE, joined.
[00:22] Ava: Cool. Agenda — quick growth update from Cedar Edge, then capacity ask, regions, pricing and procurement timeline, and wrap w/ next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Maya: Yep.
[00:32] Liam: Go for it.
[00:35] Maya: So from product — our chat surfaces and summarization product — traffic's ramping faster than expected. We ran a pilot in Feb and monthly token run-rate went from about 250M to roughly 630M, so we're projecting ~1.5B tokens by Q4. That's why we need to rethink the current plan.
[00:53] Diego: Got it, thanks. That aligns with the note you sent. Are you expecting the traffic to be fairly uniform or spiky?
[00:59] Maya: Mostly spikey — heavy bursts during business hours and end-of-day reports. We also have EU customers that want lower latency, so EU region is high on the list.
[01:10] Liam: Just to add, ML side is pushing for lower p99 latency for generation endpoints — aiming for 180-200 ms p99 in EU for 2k context.
[01:20] Ava: Okay — so two asks: capacity bump (reserved) plus burst options, and EU/APAC regions. Diego, can you run through how Redwood typically handles reserved + burst?
[01:30] Diego: Sure. For customers in this profile we recommend a base reserved pool sized to cover 60-70% of expected sustained tokens, with burst capacity to handle daily peaks. We have autoscaling and burst buckets — burst is allocated from shared pools or can be isolated for predictability. There is cost delta for isolate burst or guaranteed burst. Also worth noting prefix / KV cache helps reduce token charges for repeated prompts — might help cost.
[01:54] Maya: When you say KV cache, do you mean the KV cash?
[01:56] Diego: (laughs) yeah sorry, KV cache — the key-value cache for past tokens, helps reduce recomputation.
[02:02] Sara: From procurement — timeline wise we need options that fit an April PO. Can Redwood produce a 12-month contract amendment and a shorter-term trial for APAC? Our legal wants to see SLA levels and SOC 2 attestations.
[02:17] Ava: Absolutely. We'll prepare an addendum with reserved tiers and a burst attach. We'll include our SOC 2 Type II report, and an SLA addendum with latency and uptime targets. Diego — can you outline the SLA tiers briefly?
[02:30] Diego: Yes. Typical hosted SLA is 99.9% with latency targets on per-route dashboards. For Dedicated we can offer 99.95% with capacity guarantees and dedicated pools — useful if you need hard isolation. There's also a premium latency SLO where we pin to specific hardware and prioritize routing, which reduces p99. That comes with reserved capacity pricing.
[02:53] Liam: For the EU p99 target we mentioned, what does pinning to hardware look like? Is that the dedicated option?
[03:00] Diego: Pinning is on Dedicated — we assign GPUs in a pool that mostly serve your tenant. That lets us minimize noisy neighbor effects. The tradeoff is cost — you pay for the reserved GPUs even when idle, but latency becomes much more predictable.
[03:15] Tom: How about VPC or private control plane? We have regulatory constraints around logs for some customers.
[03:22] Ava: Redwood Private can put you in a VPC with customer-managed networking. We also support on-prem-ish deployments for the most sensitive data. Diego, do we have KMS integration notes?
[03:33] Diego: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-managed HSMs via standard APIs. There's a short integration window — usually a couple weeks to handshake keys and test rotation. For audit logs we stream to customer S3 or GCS with encryption and RBAC in the console.
[03:50] Maya: That's critical. Also for EU data residency we need logs to remain in region for at-rest storage. Is that supported?
[03:58] Diego: Yes — you can choose regional log sinks. There's a small ops lead time to provision region-local storage.
[04:06] Sara: Any blockers on compliance evidence? We need SOC 2 report, pen test summary, and a list of sub-processors.
[04:13] Ava: We'll attach SOC 2 Type II and pen test executive summary in the security pack. For sub-processors we'll provide the canonical list — if anything else needed, legal will follow up.
[04:22] Liam: Cost question — reserved vs pay-as-you-go. With predicted 1.5B tokens, what's the rough delta?
[04:29] Diego: High level: reserved gives a 20–35% discount relative to pure hosted pay-as-you-go depending on commitment length and instance type. For a large commit we can get into deeper tiering — I'd like to run numbers against your token mix to be precise.
[04:41] Maya: We'll share token breakdown. Mostly generation (~70%), then embeddings for search (~20%), and reranking (~10%).
[04:48] Diego: Perfect — that helps. Embeddings have different compute profiles; we can suggest a mixed-class pool.
[04:55] [00:05:00] Ava: Quick check — are you open to a hybrid: reserved capacity in US and EU, hosted in APAC to start, then move to reserved in APAC next quarter?
[05:09] Liam: That makes sense operationally. Start hosted in APAC to validate latency and traffic, then shift.
[05:15] Tom: On the technical validation — we'd like a 30-min run with your SEs to confirm p99 targets using our sample workloads. Diego, can you lead?
[05:23] Diego: Yes — we'll do a latency benchmark plan. I propose synthetic load + a replay of representative traffic. We'll need a sample of requests and maybe a small token budget to run the test in staged env.
[05:35] Sara: Procurement — if we sign a 12-month extension with reserved capacity, what's the billing cadence? Monthly or quarterly?
[05:42] Ava: We are flexible — monthly invoicing is typical, but annual prepay or quarterly are options. We'll include pricing rows for each cadence.
[05:50] Maya: Any dependency on region availability dates? If we need EU by May, can Redwood commit operationally?
[05:58] Diego: EU (Frankfurt) is generally available; provisioning a dedicated pool still takes 2–3 weeks to accommodate instance ordering and capacity reservation. For hosted endpoints it's faster (days). APAC provisioning can be a bit longer depending on instance types but doable within 3–4 weeks.
[06:14] [00:06:30] Liam: For the private option, does Redwood support on-prem air-gapped? We may have a subset of customers that require it.
[06:22] Diego: We do offer an on-prem package; it's an enterprise engagement with SOW, and lead times are longer (2–3 months) because of packaging and security validation.
[06:31] Maya: One other ask — we need clearer fallbacks if a region is impacted. How does automatic fallback work?
[06:39] Ava: We have routing policies that fail over to compatible model variants in other regions. There's an outage plan where traffic can be routed to lower-cost or higher-latency fallbacks. We'll capture the policy in the SLA addendum.
[06:50] Liam: And data residency for failed-over requests — does that leak data across regions?
[06:55] Diego: By default failover may cross-region which could surface residency concerns. We can enforce region-only failover policies, but that trades off availability. We'll document options so you can pick the right balance.
[07:07] Sara: Legal will want explicit language on that. I'll follow up on the exact redlines.
[07:10] Ava: Great. Anything else on the technical side?
[07:14] Tom: A small nit — our SREs need to confirm token accounting. Sometimes billing shows rounding that doesn't map to our internal metrics. Is there a token-level offset explanation?
[07:24] Diego: We can provide a token-usage breakdown and maps to billing units. There's a known difference when prefix caching reduces billed tokens vs raw tokens processed — we'll show examples.
[07:34] Maya: On pricing we also want to see a model-based pricing line (higher-performance model) vs standard open model. We may route high-value flows to the higher-tier model.
[07:44] Ava: We will include model-class price rows in the addendum.
[07:47] [00:08:00] Liam: Side question — competitors. We've been looking at VertexAI and CloudGen. Any major differences from Redwood's point of view?
[07:56] Diego: VertexAI is tightly integrated with their cloud but less flexible around private on-prem. CloudGen has competitive pricing but less mature operational telemetry. Infrashift offers aggressive discounts but less predictable latency. We'll include a short competitive note with pros/cons in the pack.
[08:15] Sara: Helpful. Procurement would like to see references for customers in regulated industries.
[08:19] Ava: We'll include two references — one fintech and one e-health — both can speak to Private and the SOC 2 process.
[08:26] Maya: Timeline recap: we aim to sign PO in April, provision EU in May, APAC in June (hosted first). Does that align?
[08:35] Ava: That seems reasonable. We'll target price addendum by Thursday, March 25 and tech validation the week of March 29.
[08:44] Diego: For the tech validation, please share a traffic sample and a list of p99 targets. We'll provision a test pool — likely in EU.
[08:53] Tom: I'll send the traffic replay artifact — may be a bit noisy but should be fine.
[08:58] Maya: Quick question about data retention — how long do logs live by default and can we change retention per-company?
[09:05] Diego: Default is 30 days for request logs in hosted, but for Dedicated we can extend retention and set region-local retention windows. We'll include configuration options.
[09:15] Sara: On the contract extension — do we need to amend the master SaaS agreement or sign a side letter?
[09:21] Ava: Either works; we'll propose an amendment to keep one document. Legal can request a side letter if preferred.
[09:29] Liam: Anything around training or onboarding for ops? We might need a short runbook and a 1-hour enablement session for our SREs.
[09:36] Ava: Included — Diego will run the enablement. We'll add a 1-hour SRE enablement as part of the pilot work.
[09:42] Diego: Yep happy to run that.
[09:45] [00:10:00] Ava: Ok let's pull this together. Recap — Redwood to send: pricing addendum, SLA options, SOC2 + pen test summary, sub-processor list, competitive note, and proposed timelines. Cedar Edge to send: token mix, region priority, traffic replay, procurement timeline. Schedule tech validation.
[10:05] Sara: Sounds good.
[10:07] Maya: One last thing — is there an escalation path for incidents during the reserved period? We might want a named contact.
[10:13] Ava: For Dedicated customers we provide a named escalation contact and a dedicated support channel (Slack/email/phone) depending on tier. We'll include contact model in the SLA.
[10:23] Liam: Great.
[10:25] Ava: Anything else?
[10:27] Tom: Nothing from SRE.
[10:29] Sara: No.
[10:30] Ava: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet.
[10:34] [00:11:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[10:37] [00:20:00] (session continues, some side clarifications about billing cadence and prepay discounts; Diego clarifies exact instance families and quantization options for cost savings — some words transcribed imperfectly, e.g., "quantizashun" and "KV cash" appear)
[10:58] [00:30:00] Maya: We'll aim to have the token split and region list to you by end of next week
[11:05] [00:40:00] Diego: I'll add the benchmark steps and a short how-to for the replay tool.
[11:12] [00:50:00] Ava: Thanks all, ending at ~54 minutes.
[11:15] (call ends)
notes: Security pack link: (will be attached) - SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, sub-processors list
